headline: Orphaned Walrus Calf Finds New Home After Dramatic Alaska Rescue
meta_description: A 5-month-old Pacific walrus orphaned on an Alaska beach receives specialized care at SeaWorld Orlando after a remarkable rescue effort.
summary_short: Discovered alone and vulnerable on a remote northern Alaska beach, a young walrus calf named Annautaq now thrives under expert care at SeaWorld Orlando.
body:
When wildlife research intern Violet Anniskett and US Geological Survey scientist Tony Fischbach discovered a 5-month-old male walrus calf hiding between the skeletal remains of two adult walruses on a remote northern Alaska beach, time was running out. Scavenging birds circled overhead. The calf's mother had departed with the herd during heavy surf, leaving him orphaned and defenseless. Named Annautaq—meaning "axe" in Iñupiaq, after Anniskett's father—the 220-pound calf faced near-certain death without intervention. Today, he's thriving at SeaWorld Orlando, one of only four US institutions equipped to house walruses, receiving up to six bottle feedings daily and around-the-clock veterinary care.

Annautaq's journey from that desolate Alaska beach to Florida spanned 4,000 miles and required an extraordinary network of people. Local community members provided initial care over several days before he was flown to the Alaska SeaLife Center in Seward, then transported again to his permanent home. The US Fish and Wildlife Service determined he could never survive in the wild—Pacific walruses depend entirely on their mothers' milk during their first year and require maternal guidance to develop essential survival and social behaviors.

At SeaWorld Orlando, Annautaq is settling into a herd of four walruses, including 2-year-old Uki, herself a rescued animal. Curator Jim Kinsler noted that Kaboodle's experience with rescued calves and Uki's companionship create an ideal environment for learning and growth. Beyond personal recovery, Annautaq carries a larger mission: alongside his fellow residents, he will help educate the public about the challenges facing Pacific walruses in an increasingly fragile Arctic. His rescue underscores why specialized marine mammal rehabilitation capacity remains essential.
quick_facts: 5-month-old male walrus calf discovered alone on northern Alaska beach
Named Annautaq, weighing approximately 220 pounds at rescue
Transported 4,000 miles to SeaWorld Orlando, one of four US walrus facilities
Receives up to 6 bottle feedings daily during specialized quarantine care
Lives with three other walruses, including rescued 2-year-old Uki
